provenance: Corrections to the imported OpenTyria tables in messages.json, from the two sources that can actually arbitrate: our own captures of client build 38797, and the client's own message-format tables recovered from Gw.exe (see studies/msgtable/FINDINGS.md). Kept beside messages.json rather than inside it so that regenerating the imported catalog cannot silently revert a verdict the client already gave us. Applying every entry here leaves zero residual disagreement between our catalog and build 38797's tables. NOTE ON RISK: the codec reads only `fields`; `declared_unpack_size`, `variable_length` and msg_header `length` are metadata it never consults. Of these entries, only GAME_SMSG 140, 146 and 421 change a field list, and Rurik sends none of those three -- so adopting this file changed no behaviour. Its value is that the catalog stops disagreeing with the binary, so later work is not built on a wrong flag. ADDED 2026-08-10: seven GAME_CMSG entries carrying `name` and the evidence for it, from two labelled input runs (toolkit/authsrv/labelrun.py, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md). The catalog had field layouts for 194 GAME_CMSG opcodes and names for NONE of them. These change NO field list -- the layouts are copied verbatim from messages.json and already agree with the client's own tables -- so they cannot affect decoding; they record what a message MEANS, which the binary's marshalling types cannot say. In particular 0x0040's u32 typing is correct and was nearly 'fixed' to float: the values are floats, the wire type is not, and the client's own SEND table says u32.

2.why: variable_length is false on this build. The binary's own fixed/variable determination is 'contains a type 7 (wide string), type 11 (array length prefix) or type 12 (nested-struct repeat count) cmd'. Our flag is true only because the importer treats `blob` as variable, but a blob is a type-5 cmd -- a fixed `count`-byte payload with NO length prefix on the wire (SPEC section 2; wire-size switch at VA 0x7dcec4 family). 144.why: INSTANCE_LOAD_REQUEST_PLAYERS is 19 bytes on this build, not the imported 18. Decoding it as 18 left one byte in the stream and every following message was misframed: the decoder read 0x1201 (out of range) and abandoned the rest of the frame, so everything the client said after REQUEST_PLAYERS was invisible. 38.name: ATTACK
38.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C4 and C9. The operator was prompted to attack a targeted hostile and the client sent this with that agent's id, immediately after 0x00C1 selected it. It is ATTACK and not a general interact: prompted to TALK TO a friendly NPC the same client sent 0x0039 instead, and clicking a player sent neither. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl step `attack`, vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T160945-c1.jsonl steps `target_npc`/`interact_npc`/`target_player`.

57.name: INTERACT
57.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C9. Sent when the operator clicked and then talked to a friendly NPC -- once with the select, three more on repeated interaction, always carrying that NPC's agent id. Clicking a PLAYER produced target-select alone and no 0x0039, so this is about interactable agents rather than about clicking. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T160945-c1.jsonl steps `target_npc` and `interact_npc` (agent 45).

61.name: MOVE_SET_HEADING
61.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C5. Field 3 (the second vec2) is a DIRECTION, not a position: across 8 samples in a session where the character COULD NOT MOVE -- so field 1 never changed -- its magnitude held at 766.8 +/- 0.4% while its angle swept the compass. A fixed-length rotating vector is a heading. This corroborates OpenTyria's TURN_TO_DIRECTION from a property the schema itself does not state. Field 4 is a small integer 1..8 whose meaning is UNVERIFIED -- it looked like an eight-way compass across 11 consecutive samples in one window and collapsed across all 26 (value 1 spans 0.0-359.1 deg), so it is NOT the absolute heading. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl, vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T160945-c1.jsonl.

64.name: MOVE_UNKNOWN_FLOATS
64.why: PARTIAL. Fields 1 and 2 are marshalled as u32 -- which is what the client's own SEND table says, so the typing here is CORRECT and is not a bug -- but their VALUES are IEEE-754 float32. Field 2 is exactly 1.0 in all 12 observed samples; field 1 takes 0.0, -0.688, -1.946, -3.018 and both infinities, and +/-inf rules out an angle in radians while fitting a ratio that crosses vertical. WHAT IT MEANS IS UNVERIFIED. It accompanies MOVEMENT, not the camera: studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C11 retracts C7 -- a prompted camera-only step sent NOTHING, and every occurrence sits between 0x003D heading updates and 0x0047 move-cancel. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl `camera`, vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T160945-c1.jsonl `merchant` and `gateway`.

70.name: USE_SKILL
70.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C1. Field 1 is the SKILL ID, not the skillbar slot, and field 3 is the target's agent id. THREE witnesses: the operator named the two skills they cast before any payload was decoded; the client's own skill and string tables resolve 153 and 105 to 'Vampiric Gaze' and 'Deathly Swarm'; and the tape's own 0x00DA SKILLBAR_UPDATE declared the bar as [153, 105, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]. Pressing slots 1 and 2 sent 153 and 105 -- a slot index would have sent 0 and 1 -- and pressing the EMPTY slot 8 sent nothing at all, so the client validates occupancy locally. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl steps `skill_1`, `skill_2`, `skill_8`.

100.name: CHAT_SEND
100.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C2 and C10. Field 2 carries the typed text VERBATIM, including the channel prefix the CLIENT adds itself: typing `rurik one` sends `!rurik one`. EMOTES GO THROUGH THIS SAME MESSAGE as literal text (`/dance`, `/sit`, `/me waves`), so they are not a separate wire message and /sit is not distinguished from /dance in shape. Field 1 is the current target's agent id for slash commands and 0 for plain chat -- 6 samples across two sessions, two maps and three target allegiances, no counterexample. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl `chat_say`/`emote_dance`, vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T160945-c1.jsonl `emote_sit`/`emote_dance`/`chat_all`/`chat_me`.

193.name: TARGET_SELECT
193.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C3, CORROBORATED across three allegiances. Field 1 is the agent to select and 0 CLEARS the selection. Three Tab presses cycled 276 -> 273 -> 274; clearing sent 0; and it preceded every USE_SKILL, every ATTACK and every INTERACT with the matching id. Seen for a hostile, a friendly NPC and another player with no difference, so it is target-select and nothing more. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl `target_tab`/`target_clear`/`attack`, vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T160945-c1.jsonl `target_npc`/`target_player`.

140.why: Our table stops one field short. Binary cmds[] @VA 0x00bfff98 (file offset 0x7fef98) is [0x0000008c, 0x00000404, 0x00000404, 0x00000104]; the MsgFormatRecv entry @VA 0x00bc93a0 (file 0x7c83a0) statically holds count=4, i.e. cmds[0]+3 fields, and the next cmds[] array begins exactly 4 dwords later, so there is no room for more or fewer. Slots 1..3 are zero in the file and are written by the MSVC dynamic initializer at VA 0x00464650-0x0046466e (`a1 74 f8 bf 00 / a3 9c ff bf 00` etc.), copying the statically-present constants [0x00bff874]=0x404, [0x00bff878]=0x404, [0x00bff87c]=0x104. cmd 0x104 = type 4, count 1 = a 1-byte unsigned int (our `byte`). We are missing that trailing byte, so we frame this message as 10 bytes when the client writes 11 and every later message in the datagram shifts.

146.why: Our table stops one field short. We are missing that trailing word: 12 bytes on the wire, not 10.
